findings.title: Dropping the build-wide lock makes GetIndex+BuildIndex non-atomic; same key can be built concurrently
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for its entire duration; it now only locks while inserting the finished index into b.cache. The check in GetIndex and the build/insert are therefore not atomic: two goroutines building the same NamespacedResource (e.g. a watch event handled via handleEvent -> getOrCreateIndex racing a concurrent Search for a namespace that was not pre-built at startup, or two concurrent Searches for a cold namespace) will both build a complete index. One result then silently overwrites the other in the cache, leaking the losing index (for file-backed indexes, an open bleve index whose handles are never closed). Worse, when size > FileThreshold both goroutines call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory, and the second open fails on the store's directory lock, so one caller gets an error even though the index is being built. Consider a per-key lock, singleflight, or an inflight-builds map so concurrent builders for the same key share one build while different keys still build in parallel.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without holding cacheMu and now runs concurrently with cache writes
findings.body: TotalDocs loops over b.cache without taking cacheMu. This PR adds a new caller: searchSupport.init now logs s.search.TotalDocs() (search.go) immediately after starting the watch-event goroutine, and that goroutine can concurrently trigger BuildIndex via handleEvent -> getOrCreateIndex, which writes to b.cache under cacheMu.Lock. An unsynchronized map iteration racing a map write causes a fatal, non-recoverable 'concurrent map read and map write' runtime panic. TotalDocs should acquire b.cacheMu.RLock() for the duration of the iteration.

findings.title: Init failure in NewResourceServer leaks already-initialized resources
findings.body: When s.Init(ctx) fails, NewResourceServer returns nil, err without any cleanup: the cancellable context created a few lines above is never cancelled (cancel is otherwise only invoked via Stop), the lifecycle backend initialized by lifecycle.Init (e.g. the SQL backend's open DB) is never stopped, and if the failure occurs in initWatcher after search.init succeeded, the watch goroutine started inside search.init runs on context.Background() and keeps polling forever. The error path should call s.cancel() and, when lifecycle was initialized, lifecycle.Stop (or otherwise unwind the partial initialization).

findings.title: Stop() no longer blocks requests: handlers dropped the Init/initErr check
findings.body: Every gRPC handler previously began with `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { return ... }`, which surfaced s.initErr — including the 'service is stopping/stopped' values written by Stop(). With those guards removed, s.initErr is never read after construction, so Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Search/PutBlob keep serving against the backend even after Stop() has been called; the stopped-state logic in Stop() is now dead code (and its unsynchronized writes to initErr race with any concurrent Init). Either restore a cheap initErr check in the handlers or remove the initErr mutation from Stop to avoid implying a shutdown guard that no longer exists.
